Interface PrimitiveTargetTypeConverter<S,T>

Type Parameters:
S - The source type
T - The target type
All Superinterfaces:
TypeConverter<S,T>
public interface PrimitiveTargetTypeConverter<S,T> extends TypeConverter<S,T>
A TypeConverter that converts to a primitive without boxing it. The find methods return an empty value, after rejecting the value in the context, when it does not convert, like TypeConverter.convert(Object, Class, ConversionContext); the get methods throw a ConversionErrorException instead.

The default implementations box through TypeConverter.convert(Object, Class, ConversionContext), so of(TypeConverter) adapts any converter; a converter that parses the primitive itself overrides them. The int methods are meant for a converter to Integer, the long methods for one to Long, and so on: a converter resolved by a conversion service does not convert to the primitive of another type, like a value that does not convert; another converter is called with the wrapper type as its target type, and a result of another type is not converted.

Since:
5.3.0

    • primitiveParser

      default @Nullable PrimitiveTargetTypeConverter<S,T> primitiveParser()
      The converter that converts to primitives itself, without calling TypeConverter.convert(Object, Class, ConversionContext), which a caller may call with a context that does not record errors, e.g. ConversionContext.DEFAULT; or null if the primitive methods box through TypeConverter.convert(Object, Class, ConversionContext), which needs the context of the argument. A converter that parses the primitive returns itself; a resolved converter returns the one it holds when that one does.
      Returns:
      The converter, or null
